description: Coding task: stop a Flask webhook service from sending duplicate customer texts. Two decisions with reasons and rejected options, a number, a command and a SQL statement to reproduce verbatim, a corrected retention value, a renamed module, an abandoned scratch folder and a fake secret pasted into the chat.

probes.question: What did we decide about remembering which webhook events were already processed, why, and which alternative did we reject?
probes.answer: We decided to record processed events in a Postgres table, webhook_events, keyed on event_id with a unique constraint. The insert is the idempotency check: a new row means process the event, and a conflict means skip it. We chose this because there is no Redis, the platform team will not provision one before next quarter, Postgres is already run locally, and the insert is atomic so two workers cannot both win. Redis SETNX with expiry and an in-memory set were both rejected (see the next answers).

facts.fact: Record each event_id in a Postgres table webhook_events with a unique constraint
there is no Redis available and the platform team will not provision one before next quarter

probes.judge_notes: Covers the Postgres unique-constraint decision, the no-Redis constraint, and the rejected SETNX option; no contradictions.

probes.question: What did we decide about stopping the carrier's timeouts and retries, why, and what did we rule out?
probes.answer: We decided the handler should return fast so the carrier does not time out and retry. It reads the raw body, verifies the HMAC, rejects timestamps older than 324 seconds, and inserts the event_id into webhook_events. If the insert is new, it submits notify_customer to a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) and returns 202. Duplicates return 200 with no notification, so the carrier stops retrying them. We ruled out Celery in front of the handler because it needs a broker, which the user cannot add.

facts.fact: Send the notification from a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) and return 202 immediately
the carrier retries when the response takes too long, and a thread pool needs no new infrastructure

probes.judge_notes: The thread pool and 202 are stated, but the answer never says a thread pool needs no new infrastructure; Celery rejection is covered.

probes.question: Which option did we rule out for recording processed event ids, and what was the reason?
probes.answer: Two options were ruled out. Redis SETNX with an expiry was rejected because it needs a new service to run, and the platform team cannot provide one. An in-memory set of seen event ids was rejected because it is lost on restart and not shared between workers, so duplicates would still get through.

facts.fact: there is no Redis available and the platform team will not provision one before next quarter

probes.judge_notes: Rejection of SETNX for needing a new service the platform team cannot provide is stated; the in-memory option is extra.

probes.answer: 324 seconds. Webhooks with a timestamp more than 324 seconds old are rejected.
probes.judge_notes: Gives 324 seconds as the replay tolerance.
